order_of_magnitude: seconds. Lifetime set by reaction with ambient CO, CH4 and VOCs.
reference: Lelieveld, Gromov, Pozzer and Taraborrelli, Global tropospheric hydroxyl distribution, budget and reactivity, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 16:12477, 2016

order_of_magnitude: hours. Dominated by OH addition during daylight.
reference: Atkinson and Arey, Atmospheric degradation of volatile organic compounds, Chem. Rev. 103:4605, 2003

order_of_magnitude: hours. Photolysis and OH reaction, both fast in daylight.
reference: Atkinson and Arey, Chem. Rev. 103:4605, 2003; Seinfeld and Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd edition, 2016

order_of_magnitude: minutes to hours in the photostationary state with NO2 and O3; the value here is for the NOx family rather than for NO alone.
reference: Seinfeld and Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd edition, 2016

order_of_magnitude: hours. OH reaction to HNO3 in daylight, heterogeneous loss at night.
reference: Seinfeld and Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd edition, 2016

order_of_magnitude: about a day. Photolysis, OH reaction and efficient wet removal.
reference: Finlayson-Pitts and Pitts, Chemistry of the Upper and Lower Atmosphere, 2000

order_of_magnitude: one to two days in the boundary layer. Oxidation to sulphate plus dry and wet deposition.
reference: Seinfeld and Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd edition, 2016

order_of_magnitude: days. Removal dominated by wet and dry deposition rather than chemistry.
reference: Seinfeld and Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 3rd edition, 2016

order_of_magnitude: about a week for submicron aerosol in the lower troposphere, set by wet removal.
reference: Textor et al., Analysis and quantification of the diversities of aerosol life cycles within AeroCom, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 6:1777, 2006

order_of_magnitude: about ten days against OH at typical mid-latitude oxidant levels.
weeks in the free troposphere, much shorter in a polluted boundary layer. The value here is the tropospheric burden lifetime.
reference: Young et al., Pre-industrial to end 21st century projections of tropospheric ozone, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 13:2063, 2013

order_of_magnitude: weeks in the cold free troposphere, hours in a warm boundary layer; the value here is the reservoir lifetime that makes PAN a long-range NOx carrier.
reference: Fischer et al., Atmospheric peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN): a global budget and source attribution, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 14:2679, 2014

order_of_magnitude: about two months against OH. The longest-lived species here.
